best_for: Java developers and ops teams who need a free, certified Java 21 runtime with a published support date, on or off AWS.

points.title: Free Java 21 with a long runway
points.text: Corretto 21 is Amazon's build of OpenJDK 21. Amazon plans quarterly updates, with its last planned update in July 2030 and end of life in October 2030.

points.title: No AWS account needed
points.text: It is free to use and redistribute under GPLv2 with the Classpath Exception. Long-term support does not depend on an AWS support plan, which is only for people who want paid help.

points.title: Certified, with a few extra fixes
points.text: It passes the Java TCK, so it meets the Java SE standard. Amazon adds patches for speed and stability that have not yet reached upstream OpenJDK.

points.title: Urgent fixes between releases
points.text: Security and other urgent fixes can ship outside the quarterly cycle when they are ready, so check for updates more often than once a quarter.

points.title: Set JAVA_HOME yourself on Windows
points.text: The Windows MSI is x64, installs for the whole machine under `C:\Program Files\Amazon Corretto\`, and Amazon's guide tells you to set `JAVA_HOME` and `PATH` after the wizard.

points.title: Mac needs admin rights
points.text: The Mac .pkg comes in Intel and Apple silicon builds, needs administrator rights, and installs to `/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/`. Run `/usr/libexec/java_home --verbose` to see the path.

points.title: Linux and versions
points.text: Amazon also builds Corretto for Linux, including musl for Alpine, but this site lists Windows and Mac only. The Windows listing keeps 15 versions; macOS lists only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
